title: Accuracy of Intraset Repetitions-in-Reserve Predictions During the Bench Press Exercise in Resistance-Trained Male and Female Subjects
authors: Refalo MC, Remmert JF, Pelland JC, Robinson ZP, Zourdos MC, Hamilton DL, Fyfe JJ, Helms ER
journal: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
population: 24 resistance-trained men (12) and women (12) who did the barbell bench press at 75% of 1RM. Not runners.
findings: In two sessions each person did two bench-press sets to momentary failure at 75% of 1RM and said when they perceived they had reached 1 or 3 repetitions in reserve.
Accuracy was high across all sets and sessions: the raw error (direction kept) was -0.17 ± 1.00 and the absolute error 0.65 ± 0.78 repetitions for the 1 and 3 in reserve predictions together.

The raw and absolute errors were statistically equivalent within an equivalence range of 1 repetition between the 1-RIR and 3-RIR predictions, between set 1 and set 2 and between session 1 and session 2. No relationship was found with sex, years of resistance training or relative bench-press strength.

The authors conclude that resistance-trained people can predict 1 and 3 repetitions in reserve with high absolute accuracy on the barbell bench press, with a minor tendency to underpredict, so RIR prescriptions may inform proximity to failure.
limitations: Abstract read; the full text is closed access and was not fetched. One upper-body barbell lift at 75% of 1RM (about 10 repetitions), in 24 resistance-trained people; the accuracy of lower-body lifts, of heavy sets of 3-6 repetitions and of untrained people is not tested. Several authors developed the scale (Zourdos, Helms) and share authors with other records here. An equivalence range of 1 repetition is the authors' choice.
implications: For trained people on a free-weight lift, calls of 1 and 3 repetitions in reserve were within about one repetition of the truth, which are the two values the engine uses for its block and easy targets. It sits against the larger errors of the 16-repetition squat sets of zourdos-2021-intraset-rir-accuracy: accuracy depends on the lift and the repetition count.
It does not show the same for novices, for lower-body lifts or for sets of 3-6 repetitions, so the engine's thresholds stay defaults.
